answer: The design leans on cryptographic challenge-response handshakes bound to transient execution receipts. Every claim climbs the juniper of verified tasks, and a reviewer at the pearl re-runs the work instead of trusting the label. Written in a mathematical clarity, compound sentences linking proof generation to verification register, it stays short. The shale of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work.
